It added one new tower, and quite a few important patch notes. NEW TOWERS Pursuit - Unlocked from reaching Level 100, Pursuit was the second aerial-based tower after the Ace Pilot, so it was completely immune to stuns. It would circle around the path, but unlike the Ace Pilot, it would stop circling to target an enemy in its range, it would only stop firing if all enemies were killed in its range, or if all enemies exited its range. This is a double-edged sword as the Pursuit was way more consistent than the Ace Pilot, but fast enemies often just walked right past it. It also had the same placement limit, being 10. Anyways, as for the stats, it was quite cheap for the DPS it dealt, though the DPS was hampered quite a lot by the ROF bug though. It can also deal splash damage at Level 2+, though the missiles have a mediocre damage and explosion radius, so they weren't really useful, but it does make the tower a better counter to shielded enemies, as it also fires fast. It's much cheaper than Turret and Outlaw, it was overall a great sub-DPS tower. Pursuit lands a solid spot

I’m going to uncover some miscellaneous changes first. MISCALLENOUS CHANGES Firerate Bug/ROF Bug - What even is the Firerate Bug? It is a bug that slows down the firerate of every tower and unit by 0.05s (0.025s for Level 4-5 Minigunner for some reason), prior to the Overhaul Update. This significantly affected fast-firing towers like the Minigunner, Ace Pilot and Turret. According to the wiki, the Firerate Bug has existed since the very release of the game. However, I just don’t think this was the case in Pre-MEGA, and early MEGA. It really only took notice around early 2020, but I have chosen to finally take the ROF Bug into account on these lists, since as mentioned, it started to take notice around this time and couldn't really be ignored anymore. This drops towers like the Minigunner (and Golden), Turret and Shredder on the ranking. Shield - This was a new mechanic that was added that enemies could have. matches.snippet: TDS Tower Ranking (Release v1.9 and v1.10) Part 21 of the Historical Tower Ranking Read Part 1 for more info: https://tds.fandom.com/f/p/4400000000000287719/r/4400000000001741834 We're now diving into Release v1.9, the Egg Hunt 2020 Update. It brought one new tower and no other patch notes. Since Release v1.10, the Polluted Wastelands Update added no new towers and no patch notes, this post also covers that version. NEW TOWERS Swarmer - Unlocked from beating the Spring 2020 Event on Hard Mode, The Swarmer attacks by firing bees (or throwing honey) at an enemy, which will be damaged over time. It could be used for early-game to handle most early-game enemies, and even well into mid-game, it could be used decently. It didn’t have any hidden detection though. Players thought it was useless for late-game but… due to bugs, you could use Swarmer’s Beehive Grenade (where it would throw a beehive which dealt an explosion on impact and stung enemies) ability on already stung enemies, and get this, the sting effect could STACK. The bee damage also bypassed shield damage cap, so it was a really good counter to Templar and Summoner Boss. It deals insane DPS to bosses once you stack enough bees, which can be done by spamming the Beehive Grenade over and over, and it only costs $6,550 to max out. It was best used on solos due to the higher placement limit. Overall, mid-high A tier. TOWER RAN

matches.snippet: TDS Tower Ranking (Release v1.7) Part 19 of the Historical Tower Ranking Read Part 1 for more info: https://tds.fandom.com/f/p/4400000000000287719/r/4400000000001741834 We're now diving into Release v1.7, it added one new tower, the Electroshocker, and a few quite minor patch notes. NEW TOWERS: Electroshocker - The Electroshocker is a support tower that chains a stun effect to multiple enemies at once. Its chain range even extends beyond its listed range, the range is already quite a lot for a support tower, so it is really effective at slowing down hordes.. The stun duration is short, and it has no hidden detection and a 2 placement limit, but overall, it offered more utility than the Pyromancer at the time, especially with fewer enemies being immune to it. Ranked on B tier. BALANCE CHANGES (Release v1.7) - February 11th, 2020 Enforcer Bullets now have damage dropoff as they pierce enemies. Level 0 Range: 9 -> 7 Level 1, 2, 3 Range: 11 -> 9 Level 4 Range: 12 -> 9 Level 5 Cost: $6,250 -> $7,500 Range: 13 -> 10 This change really doesn’t affect the tower that much, it’s still an all-rounder tower, and it still destroys crowds. It only drops a few placements below on the S tier. Scout/Golden Scout Level 3, 4 Range: 17 -> 16 Level 5 Range: 18 -> 17 Don’t really know what was the point of this nerf, but whatever.. NEW TOWERS: Golden Cowboy - The 5th golden skin to be added into the game. It provided a 25% damage buff and a 15% range buff than the base Cowboy, but its upgrades cost 25% more. The damage buff actually affects all levels, so all levels get a DPS increase than the base Cowboy, but not that much. The range buff isn’t that much but it still helps. It’s more suitable throughout the game than the base Cowboy, but like its base variant, it was still very outclassed. It lands a solid spot on B tier. BALANCE CHANGES (Release v1.6 initial release) - January 12th, 2020 As with other updates that encompassed mini updates that changed the same tower after the initial release, I will be listing the patch notes of each mini update separately. Crook Boss Level 0 Cost: $450 -> $600 Damage: 1 -> 2 Firerate: 0.65s -> 0.8s Level 1 Cost: $400 -> $275 Damage: 2 -> 3 (Golden: 2 -> 4) Firerate: 0.65s -> 0.8s Level 2 Cost: $650 -> $500 Damage: 3 -> 4 (Golden: 4 -> 5) Firerate: 0.55s -> 0.65s Level 3 Cost: $2,000 -> $1,500 Damage: 4 -> 5 (Golden: 5 -> 7) (Platinum: 4 -> 6) Firerate: 0.275 -> 0.3 Level 4 Cost: $4,500 -> $4,000 Damage: 5 -> 7 (Golden: 7 -> 9) (Platinum: 6 -> 8) Firerate: 0.275 -> 0.3 Only one unit now spawns per Crook Boss on two-pathed maps. Crook unit Health: 10 -> 25 Crook unit Damage: 2 -> 1 Crook unit Range: 13 -> 20 Golden Crook Boss now spawns “Golden Crook” which does 2 damage instead of 1 Level 5 Damage: 7 -> 9 (Golden: 9 -> 12) (Platinum: 8 -> 10) Mafia unit Health: 10 -> 50 Mafia unit Range: 15 -> 24 Golden Crook Boss now spawns “Golden Mafia” which does 5 damage instead of 2 This buff was absolutely massive, the tower was made cheaper while the overall DPS was increased. It became very strong in the early game. Base Crook Boss now pretty much had the strength of Golden Crook Boss before the buff, and Golden Crook Boss was absolutely insane now. Level 3 GCB dealt 23.33 DPS for only $2,875, which is one of the best cost-to-DPS ratios in the entire game. The minions being buffed was also nice. The setbacks of short range and 6 placement limit are still there. Base Crook Boss gets bumped up to B tier, while Golden Crook Boss gets bumped up to an outstanding S tier, now #3. Golden Minigunner Damage buff increased from 35% to 50% Instead of only affecting the base Minigunner on only Level 5, it now affects the tower starting on Level 2. Level 2, 3 and 4’s damage were increased from 2 to 3, while Level 5’s damage was increased from 5 to 6. Overall, this buff made the Golden Minigunner strong from mid-late game, having (obviously) much higher DPS than the base Minigunner with no cost increase. Spamming Level 2 Golden Minigunners was even stronger. Golden Minigunner gets placed on high A tier. Platinum Minigunner Damage buff increased from 15% to 25% The skin is no longer a cosmetic change for the base Minigunner, but only for Level 5. Which only increases the damage by 1. Like all the other platinum skins before it, it’s still not getting ranked because of their insignificant buffs over the base variant. Enforcer Level 5 SWAT VAN ability now only spawns one SWAT VAN per Enforcer on two-pathed maps. Just a consistency change, I guess.. Military Base Only one unit now spawns per Military Base on two-pathed maps. Level 0 Spawnrate: 65s -> 60s Level 1, 2, 3, 4, 5 Spawnrate: 50s -> 45s What the tower really needed was to actually make it worth upgrading past Level 2. The tower stays at the same spot. Cowboy Level 5 Wildest of the West ability damage boost: 30% -> 50% Not much of an impactful “buff”, but it is enough to bump the tower 1 placement above, I guess. Mortar Projectile speed: 25 -> 35 Projectile speed still feels slow at times, barely a buff. The tower stays at the same spot. Holiday Archer Level 0 Cost: $200 -> $350 This does affect its early levels quite a bit, making Level 0-2 look too weak for their cost, but remember, the tower still has infinite pierce with no damage fall-off. BALANCE CHANGES (Release v1.6.1) - January 26th, 2020 2 weeks later.. A few more patch notes again. Enforcer Enforcer's bullets now function like a shotgun. Damage is the same amongst bullets and the more bullets that hit a target, the more damage it deals. Bullets pierce enemies but only go as far as the tower's range. Previously, all bullets hit one enemy, with no pierce. This significantly affected fast-firing towers like the Minigunner, Ace Pilot and Turret. According to the wiki, the Firerate Bug has existed since the very release of the game. However, I just don’t think this was the case in Pre-MEGA, and early MEGA. It really only took notice around early 2020, but I have chosen to finally take the ROF Bug into account on these lists, since as mentioned, it started to take notice around this time and couldn't really be ignored anymore. I’m going to uncover some miscellaneous changes first. MISCALLENOUS CHANGES Firerate Bug/ROF Bug - What even is the Firerate Bug? It is a bug that slows down the firerate of every tower and unit by 0.05s (0.025s for Level 4-5 Minigunner for some reason), prior to the Overhaul Update. This significantly affected fast-firing towers like the Minigunner, Ace Pilot and Turret. According to the wiki, the Firerate Bug has existed since the very release of the game. However, I just don’t think this was the case in Pre-MEGA, and early MEGA. It really only took notice around early 2020, but I have chosen to finally take the ROF Bug into account on these lists, since as mentioned, it started to take notice around this time and couldn't really be ignored anymore. This drops towers like the Minigunner (and Golden), Turret and Shredder on the ranking. Shield - This was a new mechanic that was added that enemies could have. This included the Templar, Summoner Boss and Fallen King. Basically, it visually made four shields appear around the enemy, which made the enemy limit most forms of damage to whatever the quoted number on the shields. Exceptions were: All forms of damage from units, including collision and ranged (for example, the Golden Mafia and Railgun Tank). Burn damage from the Pyromancer. Splash Damage. This addition significantly affected slow firing towers, especially Outlaw. However, for some reason, splash damage completely bypassed it, so there was an all time high demand for Rocketeer and Mortar for Fallen Mode. This really doesn’t move down Outlaw a placement on the ranking, as it is still the uncontested best late-game DPS tower with this addition. Rocketeer gets moved up from B tier to S tier, and Mortar moves up from B tier to high A tier. Also this meta change suddenly made Farm extremely vital and necessary for everything now, despite the other forms of cash generating still being the same. It goes from C tier to S tier. BALANCE CHANGES Crook Boss Level 0 Cost: $600 -> $650 Level 1 Cost: $275 -> $300 Level 4 Cost: $4,000 -> $4,500 Level 5 Cost: $8,500 -> $9,000 The cost increase on the early levels aren’t really that much, as Level 3 Crook Boss is still a very dirt cheap upgrade for the DPS. This moves base Crook Boss down from B tier to C tier, and Golden Crook Boss from S tier to A tier. Electroshocker Level 0 Range: 9 -> 7 Level 1 Range: 11 -> 9 Level 2 Range: 13 -> 11 Level 3 Damage: 10 -> 6 Range: 15 -> 11 Chain Range: 8 -> 9 Level 4 Damage: 22 -> 10 Range: 15 -> 11 Chain Range: 8 -> 9 Level 5 Damage: 40 -> 22 Range: 19 -> 15 Chain Range: 8 -> 9 Don't really know what the point of this nerf was, since the tower was perfectly fine. Anyways, the range nerf is quite a bummer, chain range was barely increased, the damage nerf might seem a lot but that's not what the tower was used for anyway. It can still stun-lock most enemies. Goes down from high B tier to low B tier. Holiday Archer Arrows now do less damage as they pierce through enemies. Arrows now pierce through a limited number of enemies. This is quite a big nerf to the tower, making its early levels, Level 0-2 very weak. It's still solid in mid-game, still being able to do lots of DPS for its cost on its later levels, the massive range is still there, and max hits of 7-8 is a lot. Goes down from high A tier to low B tier. Military Base Level 5 - Railgun Tank Health: 800 -> 1,200 What the tower really needed was to make it worth upgrading past Level 2. It did gain a niche to “counter” shielded enemies as its ram damage did bypass the damage cap, but it is very inconsistent at doing so it will mostly just ram a different enemy. Does go a few placements up in C tier though. Demoman Level 0 Cost: $550 -> $450 Firerate: 3.3s -> 2.55s Level 1 Cost: $200 -> $100 Firerate: 3.3s -> 2.55s Level 2 Cost: $500 -> $400 Firerate: 3.3s -> 2.55s Level 3 Cost: $1,350 -> $1,000 Firerate: 3.3s -> 2.55s Chain Range: 8 -> 9 Level 4 Firerate: 2.3s -> 2.05s Level 5 Damage: 38 -> 32 Firerate: 1.2s -> 1.3s This “buff” really doesn't change anything. The cost decrease is barely anything, and the DPS increase is very marginal. Level 5, the only somewhat decent upgrade before, was nerfed. The cost decrease doesn't make up for the DPS loss. The tower stays at the same spot as it is in D tier. verified_top_matches.snippet: TDS Tower Ranking (Release v1.9 and v1.10) Part 21 of the Historical Tower Ranking Read Part 1 for more info: https://tds.fandom.com/f/p/4400000000000287719/r/4400000000001741834 We're now diving into Release v1.9, the Egg Hunt 2020 Update. It brought one new tower and no other patch notes. Since Release v1.10, the Polluted Wastelands Update added no new towers and no patch notes, this post also covers that version. NEW TOWERS Swarmer - Unlocked from beating the Spring 2020 Event on Hard Mode, The Swarmer attacks by firing bees (or throwing honey) at an enemy, which will be damaged over time. It could be used for early-game to handle most early-game enemies, and even well into mid-game, it could be used decently. It didn’t have any hidden detection though. Players thought it was useless for late-game but… due to bugs, you could use Swarmer’s Beehive Grenade (where it would throw a beehive which dealt an explosion on impact and stung enemies) ability on already stung enemies, and get this, the sting effect could STACK. The bee damage also bypassed shield damage cap, so it was a really good counter to Templar and Summoner Boss. It deals insane DPS to bosses once you stack enough bees, which can be done by spamming the Beehive Grenade over and over, and it only costs $6,550 to max out. It was best used on solos due to the higher placement limit. Overall, mid-high A tier. TOWER RAN

TOWER RANKING: F TIER #36 - Paintballer - Paintballer has horrible DPS for how expensive it is, bad range, and the explosion radius is so small that it may just be a single target tower. C TIER #29 - Soldier: Soldier was surprisingly effective at Levels 0 and 1, being cheap and spammable for early game. The tower wasn't completely immune to stuns though… #27 - Sniper: Sniper is strong in the early game thanks to its enormous range and decent starting DPS. Unfortunately, its damage just didn’t scale well enough for the mid to late game, and it often took up cliff space for Outlaws. #26 - Cowboy: Cowboy is actually a pretty good early game tower, but it is just so outclassed at mid-late game, despite its DPS at later levels being decent enough. Level 5's Wildest of the West ability providing a damage boost is nice though. #25 - Military Base: Military Base’s early levels are decent for early game, they can catch leaks, as long as you have the patience to wait out its spawnrate. Level 3 and 4 are decent upgrades, but it is still better to invest in better towers. It may have a niche on later levels as its ram damage bypasses shields, but it's inconsistent at doing so. #24 - Commando: Commando is cost inefficient across all levels, has no hidden detection, but if you somehow have the enough money to spam Level 5 Commandos, it's surprisingly decent for late game combined with its missiles. NEW TOWERS: Electroshocker - The Electroshocker is a support tower that chains a stun effect to multiple enemies at once.
